newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes stay lower late, diffs idle.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes stay lower late, diffs idle.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices continued to fall late, with differentials flat as a major producer evaluated November supplies and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell amid thin trade.

Rumors circulated that two major West Coast refineries struck a deal for a cargo of Oriente crude for late October delivery into the West Coast. An offer stood in the market for a late Oct/early Nov delivery of Oriente, traders said.
"Foreign barrels are starting to pop up again for late October," one trader said.
NYMEX crude oil for November delivery closed down $24.38 a barrel, down 22 cents.
A major producer offered Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude at $2.00 under November WTI for October delivery.
Major bids remained $2.50 less WTI, and outright prices for the bellwether West Coast grade ended at $21.75/22.05 a barrel, 40 cents under Friday.

Unocal reported the restart of a hydrogen processing unit at its Rodeo, Calif., refinery following 10 days of planned maintenance. Line 63 remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
California heavy crude Kern River were unchanged at $16.15/16.35 a barrel.
And prices for lightly traded Wilmington crude oil held at $17.60/17.70.
